title: Counterattack
text: “Y-you’re—right, I remember you!”

“Heeey, Lord Governor~ Big Sister came from the neighboring village to let you know—some soldiers came over there too and were causing trouble, so Big Sister gave them a good spanking before coming here, but it looks like things are way worse over this way~”
Older Sister glanced around every so often, as if searching for me, I say. Incidentally, slung over her shoulder was some battered-looking noble, all trussed up and being hauled along like luggage.
“Now then, now then, if you keep up this foolishness, I’m afraid—”
“H-help m—GYAAAAAAAAAAAAH!?”
Crackle-crackle! Older Sister let loose a bolt of lightning magic right at the noble, putting on a nice little demonstration for the Three Heroes Church soldiers to see.
“Y-you wretch! What do you think you’re doing!”
The soldiers, having watched their fellow noble get electrocuted and scream bloody murder, hurled accusations at Older Sister.
“Oh my~? You don’t understand~? If you take even one more step forward, I’ll do something even more wonderful to this person here~. And once he dies, well, you’re next, aren’t you~?”
“H-hmph! Our hearts beat as one! Did you think a little sacrifice would make us retreat—”
Whoosh! Big Sister hurled her harpoon, and it landed with a satisfying thunk right in the shoulder of the noble ringleader.
“Fast Thunder.”

Crack! Lightning struck, using the harpoon as a lightning rod and landing a direct hit. The shock seemed to knock the noble clean unconscious. The Three Heroes Church soldiers, realizing their so-called representative had just been rendered combat-ineffective in the blink of an eye, went pale as sheets.
“Now what was that you said~? Won’t you say it again for Big Sister, hm~?”

She radiated a killing intent so fierce it practically screamed there would be no second warning. Watching two of their nobles get silenced and knocked out cold by Older Sister seemed to crack right through the faith of the slave-hunting soldiers of the Three Heroes Church.
“E-everyone! Retreat!”
“I-iiiiiiiiiiiiiiii!”
“Who was it that said now’s the time to storm in!”
“There’s not a scratch of damage on their side!”
“What do we do now! We’re finished!”
“Just run! Even if Seaetto has something to say about it, the Church will surely sort it out!”
And with that, the Three Heroes Church lot scattered like a bunch of spiders, I say.
“Well… I suppose that buys us a little time for a while~?”

I wonder about that. At the very least, letting survivors escape would just be a hassle later, so it was best to keep their numbers down. Now that I could tell the Three Heroes Church soldiers apart from Éclair’s faction… Aiming Lancer, go! I hurled spear after spear, skewering the slave-hunting soldiers one by one so none of them could get away!
“Gyaaa—!?”
“W-what is this!?”
“GYAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!”

Some rather large screams echoed out there. But honestly, thinking about it… that shriek sounded awfully close to Smoked Meat’s. Whether it was actually Smoked Meat or that so-called knight commander fellow, I couldn’t quite say, but based on past loops, that particular volume of screaming tended to come from one of those two. Suspicious ties to Smoked Meat, I say.
“What in the world was that!?”
Éclair stared in astonishment at the attack I had just unleashed.
“Ah, another mystery attack from who-knows-where!?”
“……So it really is, as I suspected, that the one doing this is……”
Hmm. My location hadn’t been discovered, but it seemed Éclair’s father had already guessed something.
“Father, do you have some idea who it might be?”
“Yes. It seems that for the past several days, this same mysterious attack has been sinking ships one after another at the harbors and nearby villages……”
“It appeared to be targeting only those who committed acts of brutality.”
“Indeed… Even during the chaos of this wave disaster, it struck down the monsters that appeared. And now, just as before, it seems to be acting in our favor……”
“Ohh my~”

Older Sister too was gazing off into the distance, shading her eyes with a hand, watching the attack I’d unleashed. In any case, I’d managed to punch clean through about eighty percent of them. Serves them right, I say.
“Those of you with strength to spare, please help bind the wounded fools.”
“Yes, sir!”
And so, through all that, the Three Heroes Church’s looting was handled, and the damage from the wave was considerably lessened.
“Sadeena… was it? My thanks for your assistance.”
“That mystery attack was way more impressive than Big Sister, though~”
“No, it looked more like the follow-up strike after they fled—made possible precisely because you came to our aid.”
“Oh, don’t you worry about it~ It’d help if you sent some people over to the village too, though~ Don’t you think more might be coming?”
“……True enough. It’s a situation we can’t afford to take our eyes off of.”
At Older Sister’s words, Éclair’s father let out a sigh.
“Father…… I never imagined the people of our own nation could be so foolish.”

“It’s lamentable indeed, but the damage to the territory is minor. Once word of our current situation spreads, I doubt they’ll come charging in so recklessly again. We’ll pursue accountability later, but given the circumstances, we have no choice but to have Her Majesty the Queen return to the country as soon as possible.”
His voice carried the weight of someone already dreading what lay ahead.
“Everyone! I know you must be anxious, but let us face this together, united!”
“Ohhh!”

And so, with that, Éclair’s father and the others remained alive and well, holding their defenses while working toward recovery. The Three Heroes Church’s opportunists, trying to loot amid the chaos, had taken a bitter counterattack and fled in retreat—but somehow, it felt like the makings of a civil war brewing within the nation. That was the thing, I say. In the original timeline, Éclair’s father, the able fighters, and the fishermen had all died, leaving Éclair’s territory with no strength left to fight, suffering catastrophic losses—nearly everyone wiped out except the children, who were then turned into slaves. But this time, the casualties were kept to a bare minimum, so now that they could actually fight, the conflict was likely to drag on instead. Argh, the Three Heroes Church really is a pain, I say! Whether it was my intuition… no, rather, things I’d seen and heard from the previous loop and all the loops before that—it all pointed to this being a plausible turn of events, so I simply couldn’t afford to walk away. I see, I see. Well, I suppose I’m glad I didn’t just teleport away immediately with my Portal… Still, what should I do from here, I wonder. In any case, it looked like I’d be stuck waiting for either the Three Heroes Church nobles to give up, or for the Queen to return. Éclair’s father, along with Éclair and Crocodile Guy’s father, returned to the town to hold a council while sending word out to the allied soldiers. It seemed they were petitioning the Queen, currently abroad, for an early return.
“This should reach the Queen’s ears soon enough. After that, I must hurry back to the castle and issue various orders, but……”
“Father.”
Éclair knit her brows at her father, seeming to want to convey something.
“……I know what you’re thinking. You mean to say it’s like leaping straight into the eye of the storm, don’t you?”
At her father’s words, Éclair fell silent.
“How did Aultcray seem?”

“Upon learning of the suspicious sky phenomena and the wave disaster that had appeared within the country, he wore an expression of confusion, but he was issuing orders from the castle to guard it in the Queen’s and your absence, Father. I was dispatched as reinforcements, but……”
“I doubt even he would go so far as to exploit this current chaos to pursue his own selfish agenda and march forces into this land……”

I wonder about that. Knowing Trash, I’d bet good money he’d jump at the chance to cause mischief, wouldn’t he? After all, in the original timeline, the moment Éclair’s father died, he ran wild doing whatever he pleased.
“Father, if anything, shouldn’t King Aultcray himself be the one to quell this current calamity? If he truly is the Hero of the Seven Star Staff, then—”
“Eclair.”
Éclair’s father knit his brows, his expression one of warning. Right, of course—at this stage, Trash’s staff had vanished, so he wouldn’t even be summoned by the wave.
“……Those wretched humans.”
“Shion.”
Crocodile Guy’s father was likewise glaring at Crocodile Guy as if to scold him.

“I’ve already sent word ahead to Aultcray as well. I doubt he’d try anything strange from within the castle, but it’s also true we have no idea what the radicals of the Three Heroes Church, convinced of their righteous cause, might attempt next. We’ve no choice but to maintain our defenses while proceeding. As for those we’ve taken captive, post guards to make sure none of them escape.”
“Understood!”
The town where Éclair’s father resided was also a port town. And so, everyone turned their gaze toward the sea.
“The sea is churning something fierce…… To fight amidst air so turbulent it’s as if judgment itself were being passed……”
